##### lab-unit  192.0.2.21  scope lab  wti (TACACS+) #####
# BACK-OUT of the plan for lab-unit: it puts back what the pull of 2026-10-10 14:02 showed, for the
# settings the plan changed. Use it only after the plan was done and the check was not fine.
# The unit has no rollback: each value is live as soon as its Enter is accepted, and leaving /N with
# ESC saves it. Keep the serial session open, and a second one for the check.
#
# Type this first, on lab-unit, and check the version:   /H
# The title must read "COMMAND MENU: Version 8.10": tacctl's tables are those of that command menu,
# and another version may number its pages differently: stop.
#
##### BACK-OUT, IP TABLES (replaces every entry; see the notes): lab-unit #####
# The list of the pull, 25 entries, in its order. At the /N menu type 5 and Enter, paste the block
# as it stands, then leave /N with ESC and wait for "Saving configuration to flash". It replaces
# the 25 entries the plan pasted.
<iptables>
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.100.0/23 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.20.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.28.34 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.28.34 -p udp --dport 161:162 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.28.36 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.28.36 -p udp --dport 161:162 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.31.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.40.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.50.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.60.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.70.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.90.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.120.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 192.0.2.14 -p udp --dport 161:162 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.101.0/24 -p udp --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 10.1.100.0/23 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 192.0.2.14 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -j DROP
iptables -A OUTPUT -j ACCEPT
iptables -P INPUT DROP
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -P FORWARD DROP
</iptables>
##### END OF IP TABLES: lab-unit #####
##### UNDO THESE STEPS ON: lab-unit #####
# At the unit's prompt type /N and Enter. For each step type the item numbers of its second column,
# one at a time with Enter after each, then what the arrow says. A pick: the number of the line
# that reads as shown. ESC goes back one level. A value is live as soon as its Enter is accepted.
#  1. /N  28  6  Fallback Local  -> 2 (On (All failures))   was: 3 (On (Transport failure))
#  2. ESC ESC  leave /N: wait for "Saving configuration to flash"
##### END OF STEPS #####
#
# A value that tacctl does not hold (a secret, a community) is a line that says to re-enter the one
# you keep.
# Check now: tacctl device config pull lab-unit --diff (the differences of the plan are back).
# Do not: paste anything outside the banners; paste a block into another unit; leave /N with ESC
# before the last step of the list.
# Locked out (the paste cut your session and no login works)? A superuser runs: tacctl breakglass hold lab-unit --reason "..."
# then log in on the unit's serial console as its local Administrator account,
# fix or back out, and the superuser runs: tacctl breakglass release lab-unit
